settings.title: Content translation
settings.description: On-demand translation for visitors. Translations are produced in the browser only — nothing is stored or indexed, and the original always stays authoritative.
settings.enabledHint: When on, public pages show a Translate control if the body language differs from the site language. Off by default.

engineHints.browser: Uses Chrome 138+'s on-device translation model: free, no quota, works offline, and what a visitor reads never leaves the browser. Browsers without it simply show no translate control.
engineHints.libretranslate: Self-hosted open-source instance, no key required. Public instances are heavily rate limited — run your own for production.
engineHints.mymemory: Free public endpoint, quota shared per visitor IP. Weakest quality; use only as a fallback.
engineHints.deepl: Requires a key and is proxied through the server. Good quality, billed per character.
engineHints.google: Requires a Google Cloud Translation key and is proxied through the server.
engineHints.llm: Requires a key and is proxied through the server. Best at preserving terminology, and the most expensive.
engineHints.custom: Your own relay endpoint. Request body is { texts, target, source }; response is { texts }.

settings.apiKeyHint: Stored encrypted on the server and never sent to the browser; requests for these engines are forwarded server-side. Leave blank to keep the current key.
settings.keepTermsHint: One per line. Product names, version numbers and code identifiers are already protected — add proper nouns the heuristics miss.
